gaps.sentence: I'd like ___ more time to think about your offer.
gaps.explanation: 'A little more time' means a small additional amount; 'time' is uncountable so 'a few' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the two films has been shown on television.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two films has ...' is correct for two items; 'none' is not used for two and 'both/all' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: It took a great ___ of courage to admit the mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'A great deal of courage' is the standard pattern with uncountables; 'a great number of' needs countables.

gaps.sentence: One of my shoes is tighter than ___.
gaps.hint: shoes come in pairs of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... than the other' is the pattern for two items; 'another' would suggest more than two.

gaps.sentence: ___ the students passed with good grades.
gaps.explanation: Before 'the + noun' use 'most of': 'Most of the students'; 'most the students' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: This suitcase is ___ heavy to carry.
gaps.hint: adjective + this word + to-infinitive = impossible result
gaps.explanation: 'Too heavy to carry' means it is more heavy than possible; 'very' and 'so' cannot be followed directly by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room in here for a piano.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough room' means sufficient space; the negative 'isn't' shows the space is insufficient.
'Warm enough' means sufficiently warm; 'enough' follows the adjective.
